html:
Caracalla was emperor of the Roman Empire from 211 to 217, the elder son of Septimius Severus and Julia Domna. His official name was Marcus Aurelius Antoninus; "Caracalla" was a nickname from the hooded Gallic cloak he wore.

Severus died at York in 211 and left the empire to Caracalla and his younger brother Geta together. Before the year was out Caracalla had Geta murdered, reportedly in their mother's arms, killed thousands of Geta's supporters, and had his brother's face erased from monuments and coins.

His reign is remembered for:

  • the Edict of Caracalla of 212, which made almost all free people of the empire Roman citizens;
  • the huge Baths of Caracalla in Rome;
  • a big pay rise for the army, paid for partly with a new silver coin, the antoninianus, worth less than its face value;
  • a massacre of the people of Alexandria in 215.

He admired Alexander the Great and dreamed of eastern conquest. In 217, on campaign against Parthia, he was stabbed to death by a soldier near Carrhae, on the orders of his guard prefect Macrinus, who took the throne.
